evidence.label: Launch brief
evidence.text:
Launch brief

Somebody has launched, but the page is not converting well.

What we know: signup conversion is weak, and many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies or understand how it differs from other AI tools.

The current page leans on broad "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" language. We suspect the positioning is too generic, but we do not yet have strong evidence for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem.

Prepare a stronger relaunch message for review today. Do not publish or send anything yet.

evidence.label: Company profile
evidence.text:
About Somebody

Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams. It is designed to take responsibility for moving an objective forward: organising work inside the company, bringing in outside help when needed, and staying with the job until there is a usable result.

The product is for founders who personally carry several parts of the business and need important work to keep moving without adding another tool to manage.

Positioning should stay practical and outcome-focused. Do not imply that Somebody replaces the founder or guarantees a business result.

<untrusted_content source="company_artifact:launch/page-message" origin="application_loaded">
Current launch page

Baseline
- Current headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
- Current subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."
- Current stated audience: General small businesses.
- Launch context: Somebody has launched, but the page is not converting well. Signup conversion is weak. Many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies or understand how it differs from other AI tools.
- Current positioning issue: The page uses broad "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" language; the launch brief records a suspicion that the positioning is too generic.
- Available performance evidence: Signup conversion is described as weak; visitors often leave without understanding the intended audience or differentiation. No numeric conversion rate, timeframe, traffic volume, or comparison baseline is available in the supplied records.
- Evidence gap: There is not yet strong evidence for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem.

Prioritized diagnosis — for review

1. Priority: Audience is too broad and unclear.
Evidence: The current page states its audience as general small businesses, while the launch brief says many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies.
Effect on audience and launch outcome: The intended founders may not identify the page as relevant to them, weakening message recognition and contributing to weak signup conversion.

2. Priority: Differentiation is not clear.
Evidence: The current subhead uses broad “Automate your workflows with AI” language, and the launch brief says many visitors do not understand how Somebody differs from other AI tools.
Effect on audience and launch outcome: Prospective users may not understand why Somebody is relevant or distinct, reducing the likelihood that they continue toward signup.

3. Priority: The positioning language is generic, with an important evidence gap.
Evidence: The page uses “AI manager” and “automate your workflows” language; the launch brief records a suspicion that the positioning is too generic. It also states that strong evidence about the words founders themselves use to describe the problem is not yet available.
Effect on audience and launch outcome: Generic language may fail to connect the product to the practical work-management burden of the intended audience. The missing founder-language evidence limits confidence that a relaunch message reflects how those founders describe their need.

Relaunch messaging — draft for review only

Core message
Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams. It helps keep important work moving by organising work inside the company, bringing in outside help when needed, and staying with an objective until there is a usable result—without adding another tool for the founder to manage.

Headline
Somebody: the AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams.

Subhead
Keep important work moving without adding another tool to manage.

Body
Somebody helps founders organise work, bring in outside help when needed, and stay with an objective until there is a usable result.

Intended audience
Founders running one-person companies and lean teams who personally carry several parts of the business and need important work to keep moving. This message is not framed for general small businesses as an undifferentiated audience.

Material claims and supporting rationale
- Claim: Somebody is an AI manager for founders running one-person companies and lean teams.
  Rationale: This directly addresses the prior audience problem and identifies the product’s intended user rather than using the broader “for your business” framing.
- Claim: Somebody helps organise work inside the company, bring in outside help when needed, and stay with an objective until there is a usable result.
  Rationale: These are the supplied product capabilities and make the message more concrete than “automate your workflows with AI.”
- Claim: The message is intended to communicate practical, outcome-focused support for keeping important work moving without adding another tool to manage.
  Rationale: This responds to the stated need of founders who personally carry several parts of the business and clarifies the intended distinction from generic workflow-automation language.

Why this is distinguishable from the current message
- Audience: replaces the general-small-business framing with founders running one-person companies and lean teams.
- Headline: retains the supplied product category but adds the specific intended audience instead of “for your business.”
- Subhead: replaces generic “Automate your workflows with AI” language with the practical outcome of keeping important work moving without another tool to manage.
- Body: names the supplied capabilities—organising work, bringing in outside help when needed, and staying with an objective until there is a usable result—instead of using a broad automation claim.

Measurement plan: how to determine whether the relaunch is better
Evaluate the current page and relaunch under comparable traffic and audience conditions, using the same measurement window and attribution rules. Record the numeric baseline before or at test start; no baseline values are available in the supplied records.

Primary criterion
- Signup conversion rate: completed signups divided by eligible page sessions. The relaunch is better on the primary outcome if its conversion rate is higher than the current page’s rate in a controlled comparison. Report both rates, denominators, absolute percentage-point change, and relative percent change; do not claim improvement without the observed counts and comparison result.

Diagnostic criteria tied to the diagnosis
- Intended-audience recognition: among surveyed page visitors, the share who identify the intended audience as founders running one-person companies or lean teams. The relaunch is better if this share is higher than the current page’s share under the same question and sampling method.
- Differentiation comprehension: among surveyed visitors, the share who can accurately state what Somebody helps with and how it differs from a generic AI workflow tool, using a predeclared scoring rule. The relaunch is better if this share is higher than the current page’s share.
- Qualified progression: the rate of eligible sessions that proceed to signup, reported alongside the audience definition so that any change is not treated as improvement if traffic composition differs materially.

Decision rule
Recommend the relaunch for further review only if it improves signup conversion rate versus the current page and does not worsen both diagnostic criteria. Treat results as inconclusive when traffic, audience definition, measurement window, denominators, or scoring rules are not comparable. Numeric thresholds, sample size, timeframe, and statistical decision rules remain to be set before testing because they are not supplied in the records.

Boundaries for accurate use
- Keep the message practical and outcome-focused.
- Do not state or imply that Somebody replaces the founder.
- Do not guarantee a business result, signup outcome, or any specific performance improvement.
- Do not claim that the message reflects founders’ own words; strong evidence for that language is not yet available.
- Do not present the weak signup-conversion observation as a quantified result: no numeric conversion rate, timeframe, traffic volume, or comparison baseline is available in the supplied records.
- The measurement plan defines criteria; it does not report results. No relaunch result has been measured.
- This is a draft for review only. Do not publish or send it yet.

Status: Draft for review. Do not publish or send.
